## Overall response

The review concludes that the report is a strong scientific summary of a
credible MSE and supports its use to continue SC14 discussion and
identify a provisional shortlist. Its central concern is consistency across
the report, CMP specifications, registries, source and public data, figures,
Slick results, and annual-application material.

The authors accept that central finding. The full MSE report, SC14 questions
and tasks paper, technical paper, and this response use the same final results.
The immediate request is for SC14 to
agree that the scientific work is sound, agree the decision criteria, identify
a provisional short list, and provide management guidance. Adoption can follow
completion of the instructions and checks needed for annual use.

## Response to the Terms of Reference

| ToR finding | Response |
|---|---|
| Design is broadly consistent with SCW17, but reported results and public files are not consistently aligned | Save one final SC14 set of results and use it to remake all public products; document how the candidates changed from SCW17 to the final comparison |
| Overall MSE structure is appropriate, but tuning, allocation, precision, performance measures, and criteria for alternative cases need further support | Put definitions and complete CMP-by-OM results in the technical paper and ask SC14 to agree the minimum biological performance requirements and how alternative cases should be used. Treat allocation analysis as complete; add the author's explanation of why the existing work is sufficient |
| Uncertainties and limitations are clear in prose but not always supported by one checkable numerical account | Add one biological-performance table, results for each component in the two-stock OMs, uncertainty due to the number of runs, effort and low-catch results, and a comparison using alternative reference points |
| A provisional shortlist may be supportable, but the supporting results and annual rules are incomplete | Ask for a provisional shortlist and a list of work to finish rather than immediate adoption |
| Material inconsistencies occur in settings, data timing, candidate membership, results, and figure construction | Require the important numbers to agree across all products before publication and identify every product that is no longer current |
| Scientific findings and management choices are not always separated | Separate minimum biological performance, results under alternative assumptions, and management preferences, and place management questions in the decision table |

## How to tell when the work is complete

### Agreement among the published files

This action is complete for `SC14-MSE-2026-RC1`. All 47 automatic checks
passed. They compare CMP settings, candidate membership, tuning, performance
statistics, time periods, labels, two-stock components, scorecard inputs,
public downloads, reported statements, and file fingerprints. The complete
results are recorded in the [checks of agreement among the SC14
files](../governance/release-check.qmd).

### Minimum biological performance requirements

The 60% dynamic Kobe-green probability remains a common tuning target,
not the only requirement for biological performance. The response should
explain how this target relates to the COMM8 objectives and should report the
chance of low biomass and overfishing. Results must be shown for each relevant
stock component and difficult OM. A decision to accept a known weakness must
be identified as a management judgment.

### Ready for annual use

Completion requires a complete set of instructions from which two independent
analysts obtain identical advice. It must address units, providers, cut-off
dates, missing and revised data, weighting, prior advice, annual limits,
rounding, allocation, realized catch, effort, fallback, verification, and ECP
rules for who reviews a problem and what action can be taken.

### Spatial results and the allocation comment

The allocation analysis is complete for this paper. The author's response will
explain the purpose of the fixed-split tests, how they relate to the allocation
method in the CMP, and why no additional allocation analysis is needed. The
spatial results remain relevant where they help SC14 understand stock
structure, movement, or regional monitoring.

### Banking and borrowing

The updated runs may be reported as work in progress. A conclusion
about the incremental effect of banking and borrowing requires a matched
without-banking-and-borrowing comparison using identical OM draws and all
other CMP settings held constant.

## Overall conclusion

> The authors thank the reviewer and accept the central recommendation that the
> scientific synthesis and its supporting products must present one consistent
> account. The MSE is sufficiently advanced for Scientific Committee
> review and provisional shortlisting. Final recommendation or adoption should
> depend on agreement of minimum biological performance requirements, instructions
> for annual use, and exceptional-circumstances items
> recorded in this response. The checks on published results are complete for
> `SC14-MSE-2026-RC1`.

The complete reviewer text will accompany this response or be submitted as a
separate official information paper. These response tables do not replace the
independent review.
